candidates.name: Markov’s Theorem Without Stabilization [6]
candidates.statement: Let X be an oriented knot type and let (X+, X−) be a pair of closed braids such that X−∈Bmin(X) and X+ ∈B(X) with b(X+) = m and b(X−) = n. Then there exist X′ + ∈B(X), X′ −∈Bmin(X), and a ﬁnite set of templates T (m, n) (whose membership is only dependent on (m, n)) such that: (1) X+ is exchange reducible to X′ + and X−is exchange equivalent to X′ −, and (2) There is a template (D+, D−) in the ﬁnite set T (m, n) where, using the same braiding assignment, on D+ and D−, the diagram D+ carries X′ + and the diagram D−carries X′ −.

candidates.name: The Bennequin Trick
candidates.statement: Let Γ ⊂R3 be an oriented differentiable graph that is transversal to the standard contact structure ξ of R3. Let e ⊂Γ be an edge having a local parameterization function f(t): [0, 1] →R3 where f(t) = (ρ(t), θ(t), z(t)). If dθ dt is not positive for all t then there exists a transversal isotopy of Γ which is the identity everywhere except on a small neighborhood of e such that for a resulting parameterization bf(t) = (bρ(t), bθ(t),bz(t)) we have dbθ dt being everywhere positive. candidates.statement: There exist inﬁnitely many transversal knot types of braid index 3 which are not transversally simple. In particular, consider the collection of inﬁnitely many pairs of transversal knots (TX+, TX−) deﬁned by the pairs of transversal closed 3–braids TX+ = σ2p+1 σ2r 2 σ2q 1 σ−1 2 , TX−= σ2p+1 σ−1 2 σ2q 1 σ2r 2 , where p + 1̸ = q̸ = r and p, q, r > 1 Then, the transversal knot types T X + and T X − associated to each pair belong to the same topological knot type and have the same β–invariant, but they do not represent the same transversal knot type.
